about: Every file under tests/corpus/files/ has one entry: what it is for (reason), how ReverbScope reads it (loader) and what must happen (expect). Synthetic entries are regenerated by generate.py; an entry from a community report names its issue.

entries.reason: The smallest canonical PCM-16 WAV: the baseline every other wav/ entry varies.
WAVE_FORMAT_IEEE_FLOAT, two channels: the format a DAW's 32-bit float export uses; channels must survive.
A LIST (metadata) chunk of odd size with its pad byte before fmt, as recorders and some DAWs write; the reader must skip it.
The same chunk without its pad byte (a writer that ignores RIFF alignment): libsndfile refuses it, and the error must be a ReverbScope error, not a crash.
data before fmt: not a readable WAV; the refusal names the file.
data size 0xFFFFFFFF, as a streaming writer or a recorder that lost power leaves it: read to the end of the file.
data size larger than the file (a truncated download or copy): what is there is read, nothing is invented.
A header without samples: refused as empty, not analysed as silence.
An odd data size, 199 bytes of 16-bit mono (a writer that miscounted): the 99 whole frames read and the last byte is dropped, not read as a sample.
fmt with 0 channels: refused before any division by the channel count.
fmt with sample rate 0: refused before any division by the rate.
WAVE_FORMAT_EXTENSIBLE declared with a 16-byte fmt (no extension): a malformed header must be an error, not garbage audio.
Format tag 0x55 (MPEG layer 3 in a RIFF wrapper): not PCM; refused with the file named.
RIFF size 0 (a writer that never went back to fill it): the chunks still read.
A fmt chunk and no data chunk (a recorder that stopped at once): refused, not read as empty audio.
One frame: reads; the analysis refuses it later as too short, with a sentence.
A float WAV with a NaN sample (a plug-in or export that failed): refused at the door so no NaN reaches the analysis or a saved file.
AIFF, as Logic Pro and Pro Tools export: read by the same reader.
AIFF with float samples (Logic's 32-bit float export).
CAF, Logic Pro's own recording format.
FLAC: a lossless export that is converted to WAV when it is copied into a session.
Wave64, the container REAPER and others use for takes over 4 GB.
RF64, the EBU container for long Broadcast WAV takes.
A sidecar re-saved by Notepad or PowerShell 5: UTF-8 BOM and CRLF line ends must still read.
Text after the JSON object (a merge marker, a pasted line): refused, not silently truncated.
sample_rate as the string "48000" (a hand edit): refused with the field named, not compared as text.
duration_s NaN (Python's json writes it, no other reader accepts it): refused, since no sweep can be built from it.
A sidecar from a later ReverbScope: refused with the version named rather than read with guessed meaning.
A JSON array where an object is required.
Valid JSON without the reverbscope_sweep key (another program's sidecar).

A session saved by 0.5.0b2 without curves, its impulse response cut to 300 samples (the loader needs the direct sound only): the baseline every other session/ entry is derived from, and a file that must open in every later version.
result.json as 0.4.x wrote it: no placement, clipping, dropouts, direct level, playback speed or energy metrics. Optional records default; the report and the health checks still render.
session.json with schema_version 0 and fields from a later version: older is read, unknown is ignored.
Both JSON files re-saved with a UTF-8 BOM and CRLF (Windows editors).
session.json saved as UTF-16 (PowerShell's Out-File default): refused with the file named, never decoded as mojibake.
result.json cut in half (a save that died, a partial download): refused with where the JSON breaks.
result.json from a later ReverbScope: refused with both versions named.
impulse_response.wav shorter than the direct sound result.json describes (a damaged copy): it loaded and the first plot failed with a bare ValueError before 0.5.0b3.
impulse_response.wav at 44100 Hz next to a 48000 Hz result: another session's file, drawn on the wrong time axis before 0.5.0b3.
session.json naming result.json outside its folder (a crafted bundle, #11): never followed.
result.json holding the NaN and Infinity tokens Python's json writes: loads; the listing shows such a number as not available rather than failing.
A zero-byte session.json (a save interrupted before the first write): refused, not read as an empty session.
session_dirs as a string was read as the three folders a, b and c.
positions as a number.
comparable as the text "false", which bool() reads as true.
A metric delta without its name: loaded and then failed in the report before #11.
A 400-digit frequency: float() of it raised OverflowError out of the loader before #11.
